hypotheses.justification: The equivalence holds for any adjunction `adj : G ⊣ F`, with no condition on F. By `isLocal`, `f : X ⟶ Y` is local for `range F.obj` iff for every `W : C` the map `(Y ⟶ F.obj W) → (X ⟶ F.obj W)`, `g ↦ f ≫ g`, is bijective. Transport this map along the bijections `(adj.homEquiv _ W).symm`. By `Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm` it becomes `h ↦ G.map f ≫ h` from `(G.obj Y ⟶ W)` to `(G.obj X ⟶ W)`. So f is local iff precomposition with `G.map f` is bijective for every `W : C`. By Yoneda this holds iff `G.map f` is an isomorphism. Concretely: surjectivity at `W = G.obj X` gives `r` with `G.map f ≫ r = 𝟙`. Injectivity at `W = G.obj Y` then gives `r ≫ G.map f = 𝟙`. The converse is clear. Fullness is not used anywhere in this argument. The current proof uses it only through `isLocal_adj_unit_app` and `isIso_of_fully_faithful`, and the direct argument above replaces both. This entry and the `[F.Faithful]` entry can be removed separately, and also together.

Same argument as for `[F.Full]`. The bijection `(Y ⟶ F.obj W) ≃ (G.obj Y ⟶ W)` given by `adj.homEquiv`, with naturality from `Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm`, turns locality of f for `range F.obj` into bijectivity of precomposition with `G.map f` on every `Hom(-, W)` with `W : C`. By the Yoneda argument this is equivalent to `IsIso (G.map f)`. Faithfulness of F is never needed. It is used only by the current proof (`isLocal_adj_unit_app`, `isIso_of_fully_faithful`), which can be replaced by this direct argument. It can be removed on its own, or together with `[F.Full]`.
